author: WhyOS-Apps contributors
description:
Keep texts you type often (an address, a long command, a greeting) and
let the badge type them for you. Connect a computer to the bottom USB-C
port, click where the text should go, and press Enter on a snippet: the
badge types it as a USB keyboard, new lines and tabs included.

A text can hold keys and shortcuts too: Esc, F5, Ctrl+C, Alt+Tab,
Win+R, and a pause for a window to open. In the editor, Shift with a
key such as Esc or an arrow, or Ctrl or Alt with any key, puts it in;
the square opens Insert key, to choose modifiers and a key.

Each text (a snippet) has a name for the list and up to 1000 bytes of text. The
triangle key adds one, the cross edits it, the square has the options
(type, edit, move, delete). Esc stops a text being typed.

A USB keyboard sends keys, not characters, so tell the app the
computer's keyboard layout (cloud key): US, US International or US on a
Mac. With the last two, accented letters and the euro sign are typed
too; they can only be put in a snippet by editing its file
(snippets.txt in the app's settings folder) over SSH.

The first row, Mouse, makes the badge the computer's mouse: the arrows
move the pointer (a tap is one pixel, holding goes faster), Enter is
the left button (hold it to drag), the cross a right click, Fn+Up/Down
scrolls. Keep awake (the triangle) moves the pointer a pixel and back
every 30 seconds while the app is open, so the computer does not go to
sleep or show you away. The mouse needs WhyOS from 2026-10-20 or later.

The badge only shows up as a keyboard or mouse with the side port (J1)
unplugged. The texts are stored as plain text on the badge: keep
passwords out of it.

launch.info: type saved texts, move the mouse

name: HIDeous
summary: Saved texts the badge types on a computer, and the badge as its mouse
